---
title: "Current implementation"
---

## Package boundary

Cellerator is an early biological machine-learning framework. Models can use
measurements, identity-addressed sparse fields, molecular events, regulatory
relations, latent representations, spatial environments, or combinations of
these. A general `Cell` binds cellular identity and caller-owned information
to an optional shared learned program. Explicit state transitions use
`DynamicalCell` and `DynamicalModel`; the legacy `Model` name aliases the latter.
PyTorch supplies the current ordinary training integration while native
operations and arbitrary representations remain first-class.

Implemented facilities have different backend and maturity boundaries. The 2026-10-29 framework expansion adds executable CPU reference mechanisms, C++ classes, optional bindings, and CUDA sources. A source file or namespace does not by itself establish numerical qualification, biological validity, or a performance advantage. In particular, topology planning and callback-based execution do not establish an autonomous distributed GPU service.

## Available package surfaces

- `modeling` provides a general `Cell` information/program handle and explicit `DynamicalCell`/`DynamicalModel` transitions, step contexts/results, observations, and experiments. Legacy dynamic construction remains deprecated compatibility behavior. The package imports without Torch or a native extension.
- `nn` and `torch.nn` expose bound `FeatureEncoder`, dense/packed/CSR `RelationAttention`, reusable `PreparedRelation`, shared `InteractionPrograms`, `FeatureReadout`, labelled `ModelWithViews` queries, supervision helpers, biological manifests, and functional/module grouped linear composition. The Torch-free root provides model-local `FeatureBinding` and borrowed-value prediction/query records. Ordinary Torch parameters and optimizers remain ordinary; existing canonical native owners retain their guarded update contracts. The source examples cover masked expression, causal event history, and paired auxiliary readouts.
- `state`, `events`, and `dynamics` provide sparse/ragged/layout-aware state, generation-safe store references, event histories and trajectories, lineage, discrete/continuous/stochastic reference dynamics, and explicit composition. Quantization profiles can be shared across cells and feature orderings; exact-value overrides remain per-payload and caller-controlled.
- `interactions` provides directed, bipartite, and joint hyperedge computations with explicit activity gates, aggregation, and native sparse worklist adapters. Native model, relation, layout, and field classes preserve semantic identities independently of storage slots. Incremental native execution invalidates declared dependencies and caches unaffected results.
- `execution` provides populations, routed context, suspension/resumption, lifecycle effects, expert-major worklists, topology cost estimates, revisioned parameter residency, and asynchronous callback execution. Native conditional dispatch preserves exact expert revisions and origin identities. Logical routing, biological accessibility, and physical placement remain separate.
- Optional Torch adapters provide learned dynamics, overlapping interactor modules, sparse expert execution, and differentiable distributed dispatch. CPU Gloo execution has focused two-process evidence; GPU/NCCL and multi-host execution remain unqualified. The collective adapter requires coordinated rank participation and is distinct from independently scheduled expert callbacks.
- `spatial` provides an incremental neighborhood index and conservative pairwise scalar diffusion. `inference` provides observation-conditioned particles and bounded event-history search with explicit uncertainty and search limits.
- Experimental accessibility, inheritance, and response-sensitive precision policies compose with these mechanisms. They encode caller-supplied assumptions; no universal gene ON/OFF biology or inherited regulatory program is imposed.
- Optional native CUDA resources and numerical operations use explicit streams, device views, compact worklists, FP16/FP32 contracts, and caller-visible storage. Sparse attention and segmented expert linear execution expose backward operations; packed embeddings consume selected state codes without dense decoding; supplied molecular events update sparse stoichiometry; word-mask and experimental bitplane gates evaluate explicit regulatory rules. An exact-revision host-to-device transfer bridge retains parameter leases. These new SM70 paths now have bounded V100 numerical evidence; see the validation record below. The optional ggml bridge supplies numeric block quantization independently of biological quantization profiles.
- The optional trajectory training adapter shares one trainable model across independently timed ragged states, with explicit truncation, loss reduction, gradient accumulation, and optimizer boundaries. It does not invent gradients through discrete molecular events.
- The host Python package provides native CPU Product2 and a `torch.nn.Module` adapter for CPU FP32 vectors with first-order input and coefficient gradients.
- Optional CUDA indexed-mechanism and sparse-support components have their own builds, contracts, and evidence.
- Prepared entity-to-mechanism routing is opt-in. The established Python route remains the default.
- ATen tokenization is optional and caller-directed. Gene-aware C++ tokenizer classes share an annotation-built vocabulary and retain typed ranked/event inputs; a common virtual execution signature remains deferred. Tokenization does not assign biological interpretation to tokens or events.
- `ExecutionField` is an experimental CPU composition of prepared Product2 operations. It has explicit structure rebinding, but no JIT, live recompilation, or general compiler contract.
- AnnData is a required Python dependency. Its new adapter maps explicit `X`, layer, or raw inputs to identity-aligned state and writes aligned observations while preserving sparse inputs. Classical single-cell analysis remains upstream in Scanpy and RAPIDS-singlecell.

Start with the [NN foundation guide](nn_foundation.qmd), [biological framework guide](biological_framework.qmd), [distributed execution contract](distributed_execution.qmd), and [native CUDA guide](framework_cuda.qmd). The [Python binding guide](development/python-bindings.md), [sparse-support reference](sparse_support_foundation.qmd), [tokenization reference](tokenization.qmd), and [experimental fields note](development/experimental-fields.md) retain their narrower contracts. The [source routing guide](development/routing.md) identifies owners; the [developer reference](developer_reference.qmd) describes established build and validation routes.

## NN foundation evidence, 2026-10-31

The biological-meaning pass connects canonical biological identities, actual
model indices, and repeated occurrences to neural construction and supervision.
Prepared relations bind endpoint order, grouping, optional existing axes,
structural generation, and device independently of mutable features. Queryable
readouts preserve output identities and require actual registered numerical
conditioning; descriptive context does not count as conditioning. Explicit JSON
manifests preserve declarations beside weights without changing native-owner
checkpoints or reconstructing executable code.

The [integration qualification](../planning/nn-biological-meaning-2026-10-31/VALIDATION.md)
records CPU integration, synthetic expression/history and auxiliary training,
isolated wheel/import checks, and documentation rendering. Its
[bounded V100 run](../planning/nn-biological-meaning-2026-10-31/gpu/REPORT.md)
passed all six tests with zero skips and verified scheduler cleanup. This checks
new compositions and prepared device structures, including FP16/FP32 attention
VJPs and native grouped-linear interoperability. It does not qualify performance,
scientific biological validity, distributed service, or C++ modeling parity.
Numerical kernels and native bindings were preserved by this pass.

`GatedInteractor` now rejects supplied context unless a declared conditioning
path consumes it. Its `context=None` computation is preserved. This is an
intentional compatibility repair for callers that previously supplied ignored
context. Raw neural and CSR APIs, generic cells, explicit dynamics, and native
parameter-owner/checkpoint contracts remain available.

The first NN milestone supplies composable biological feature/interaction
modules, shared trainable readouts, generic cell binding, a compatibility
migration for explicit dynamics, and a native grouped-linear autograd adapter.
The [qualification record](../planning/nn-foundation-2026-10-31/VALIDATION.md)
records the combined CPU suite, native CPU composition, package validation,
and their limits.

The [CUDA adapter qualification](../planning/nn-foundation-2026-10-31/grouped_linear/REPORT.md)
passed all 13 tests on admitted V100/SM70 hardware with zero skips. A separate
admitted memcheck run passed the same 13 tests with zero reported errors;
both jobs verified resource cleanup. Checks cover input and weight VJPs,
FP16/FP32 operands, FP32 master weights, empty/ragged segments, streams,
mutation rejection, and composed ordinary-layer training. These are bounded
correctness and memory-access checks, not a speedup or biological claim.
The native numerical kernels and bindings were reused unchanged.

## Framework expansion evidence, 2026-10-29

Focused source-package tests, native C++ tests, optional binding checks, runnable
examples, and a CPU wheel build accompany the additions. The combined host
build includes modeling, conditional dispatch, and the optional pinned ggml
bridge. The new CUDA implementation has admitted V100 numerical runs for all
eleven smoke programs and nine Python binding checks. Memcheck, racecheck,
initcheck, and synccheck each report zero errors. The
[V100 framework validation report](../planning/v100-framework-2026-10-29/REPORT.md)
records exact cases and receipts. These are focused kernel and binding checks,
not full-workload performance evidence. No speedup, production readiness,
biological validity, GPU distributed service, or complete training-system claim
follows. The earlier compile-only integration record remains in the
[implementation push](../planning/framework-push-2026-10-29/DELIVERY.md).

## Prepared routing evidence boundary

The frozen prepared-routing binary passed its 16-test correctness suite, exact CUDA correctness checks, and Compute Sanitizer memcheck, racecheck, and synccheck. The source-bound report measured a bounded lifecycle improvement for synthetic ranked `[32,8]` inputs at reuse horizon 64; the event result was inconclusive, and dense Torch was faster at larger stress shapes. Prepared routing remains opt-in, has a substantial cold-first cost, and is not evidence of a full-model or biological speedup. See the [qualification report](https://github.com/tumlinso/Cellerator/blob/94c534fc794fe8cc3e0434e4a50f379401ddbb3c/bench/sparse_support/experiments/prepared_routing/REPORT.md) and [frozen correctness receipt](https://github.com/tumlinso/Cellerator/blob/main/planning/coherence/qualification/cuda/complete-correctness-fixed-state.json).

Other source-bound sparse, tokenization, layout, and performance records retain their own workload and validation limits. The [reference and history index](experiments_and_history.qmd) routes those pages. The prior dated implementation record is preserved in [historical snapshot](https://github.com/tumlinso/Cellerator/blob/main/docs/history/current_implementation_2026-10-28.qmd).

## Gaps

Cellerator is not near complete. Distributed GPU transport integration, performance qualification of the new kernels, broad end-to-end training, richer dynamical solvers, and biological validation remain open. Residency movement and physical execution still need concrete runtime callbacks; planner costs are supplied estimates. Compiler/IR integration is not expanded by this implementation push. Keep correctness, scientific validity, usability, and performance claims separate and bounded by their evidence.
